## Purpose and Entry Points
LikeC4 is a TypeScript monorepo for authoring an architecture DSL, turning models into live diagrams, exports, editor tooling, and AI/MCP integrations. Primary user entry points are the Node CLI (`packages/likec4/bin/likec4.mjs`, `packages/likec4/src/cli/index.ts`), language server (`packages/language-server/bin/likec4-language-server.mjs`), MCP server (`packages/mcp/bin/likec4-mcp.mjs`), and VS Code extension (`packages/vscode/src/activate.ts`).

## DSL, Workspace, and Semantic Model
The Langium-based language server owns parsing, references, validation, workspace discovery, and conversion from `.c4` source/configuration into project model data. Its grammar and service wiring form the semantic boundary between user-authored DSL and runtime model objects.
- `packages/language-server/src/like-c4.langium`
- `packages/language-server/src/LikeC4LanguageServices.ts`
- `packages/language-server/src/model/model-builder.ts`

Configuration is schema-driven and supports Node-side config loading; consumers should use this layer rather than interpret project files independently.
- `packages/config/src/schema.ts`
- `packages/config/src/node/load-config.ts`

## Core Model and View Computation
`@likec4/core` is the framework-neutral domain layer: logical/deployment elements, relations, styles, view models, manual layouts, and builder APIs. It transforms parsed model/view declarations into computed node-edge graphs. Separate algorithms handle element, deployment, dynamic-flow, relationships, and project-overview views; include/exclude stages and predicates define what reaches a view.
- `packages/core/src/model/LikeC4Model.ts`
- `packages/core/src/compute-view/compute-view.ts`
- `packages/core/src/compute-view/deployment-view/compute.ts`

Manual-layout snapshots are a distinct overlay on computed diagrams, allowing user positioning without changing semantic architecture.
- `packages/core/src/manual-layout/applyManualLayout.ts`
- `packages/core/src/manual-layout/applyCachedLayout.ts`

## Layout Pipeline
Computed views are converted to graph layouts through Graphviz printers, adapters, and parsers. Graphviz can run through a native binary or WASM adapter; queueing centralizes layout work. Sequence/dynamic views have their own layout path. AI enhancement is an optional layer around graph layout rather than the source-of-truth model.
- `packages/layouts/src/graphviz/GraphvizLayoter.ts`
- `packages/layouts/src/graphviz/wasm/GraphvizWasmAdapter.ts`
- `packages/layouts/src/graphviz/ai/enhanceLayoutWithAI.ts`

## Diagram Rendering and Interaction
The React diagram package renders layouted views with XYFlow, custom nodes/edges, themes, overlays, navigation, search, and editor state machines. Public React-facing components receive model/project context; internal conversion maps LikeC4 views to XYFlow structures. Editing emits view/layout changes for persistence back through host integrations.
- `packages/diagram/src/ReactLikeC4.tsx`
- `packages/diagram/src/likec4diagram/DiagramXYFlow.tsx`
- `packages/diagram/src/editor/actor/machine.ts`

The icon catalog is a separately packaged SVG/TSX asset source used by diagram and editor consumers.
- `packages/icons/tech/index.ts`
- `packages/icons/aws/index.ts`

## Delivery Surfaces and Exports
The CLI orchestrates language services, Vite-based preview/static builds, validation, formatting, publishing, code generation, and diagram/image/Draw.io/Markdown/JSON exports. Generators translate model/view data to Mermaid, PlantUML, D2, Draw.io, Markdown, React, and TypeScript artifacts.
- `packages/likec4/src/cli/preview/preview.ts`
- `packages/likec4/src/cli/export/index.ts`
- `packages/generators/src/index.ts`

The Vite plugin exposes computed projects, exports, icons, and RPC as virtual modules, connecting dev/build hosts to the model pipeline.
- `packages/vite-plugin/src/plugin.ts`
- `packages/vite-plugin/src/virtuals/model.ts`
- `packages/vite-plugin/src/rpc/rpc.ts`

## Hosted and Editor Integrations
The VS Code extension embeds the preview, runs browser or Node language-server variants, and bridges commands/RPC. The playground is a React/Vite client with a Cloudflare Worker backend for authenticated/shared workspaces backed by KV abstractions. MCP exposes model/query/render/layout tools over stdio or streamable transports for AI clients.
- `packages/vscode/src/node/extension.ts`
- `apps/playground/worker/index.ts`
- `packages/mcp/src/server/createMCPServer.ts`

Material runtimes are Node.js, browser React/TypeScript, Vite, Graphviz native/WASM, VS Code extension APIs, and Cloudflare Workers/KV. Documentation is a separate Astro application.
- `apps/docs/astro.config.mjs`
